entries.1:1: Paul introduces himself as someone chosen and sent by God to represent Jesus, and he mentions Timothy as a fellow believer standing with him. It means this letter comes with real authority but also from a team, not a lone voice.
entries.1:2: Paul greets the Christians in Colossae as people set apart for God and genuinely part of Christ's family. He wishes them God's kindness and peace, reminding them they belong to a Father who cares for them.
entries.1:3: Paul and Timothy regularly thank God and pray for these believers. It shows that praying for others with gratitude is a normal, ongoing part of following Jesus.
entries.1:4: Their faith in Jesus and their love for other believers have been reported to Paul, and that news moves him to pray. It means the way you trust God and treat people gets noticed and matters.
entries.1:5: They keep going because of a confident expectation of what God has stored up for them in heaven, which they first heard in the message of good news. Hope gives people something solid to live toward.
entries.1:6: The good news is not just words; it is producing real change and growth all over the world, just as it did among them from the first day they understood God's kindness. It means the message still works and bears fruit in ordinary lives.
entries.1:7: They learned this message from Epaphras, a dear friend and faithful worker for Christ on Paul's behalf. It reminds readers that God often uses trusted, ordinary people to bring them truth.
entries.1:8: Epaphras told Paul about the love these believers have, a love produced by God's Spirit. It means their care for one another was real evidence of God at work in them.
entries.1:9: Since Paul heard about them, he has not stopped praying that they would clearly understand what God wants and have practical wisdom from the Spirit. It means knowing God's will is something worth praying for continually.
entries.1:10: Paul prays they will live in a way that pleases the Lord, doing good things that bear fruit and getting to know God better along the way. It means a life that honors God is both productive and growing.
entries.1:11: He asks that they be strengthened by God's mighty power so they can endure hard times with joy rather than collapsing. It means strength for suffering comes from God, not from willpower alone.
entries.1:12: They are to thank the Father, who has given them a share in what belongs to his people in the light. It means gratitude is the right response to being included in God's family and future.
entries.1:13: God has rescued them from the grip of darkness and moved them into the kingdom of his beloved Son. It means their allegiance and safety have been completely transferred.
entries.1:14: In Christ they have been set free and their sins have been forgiven. It means the debt that stood against them has been cancelled, not merely overlooked.
entries.1:15: Christ shows us exactly what the invisible God is like, and he existed before anything created came to be. It means we can know God by looking at Jesus.
entries.1:16: Everything that exists, visible or invisible, including all spiritual authorities and powers, was made through Christ and for him. It means nothing in the universe is outside his ownership and purpose.
entries.1:17: Christ existed before everything, and everything holds together in him. It means the universe is not random or self-sustaining; it depends on him moment by moment.
entries.1:18: Christ is the head of the church, its beginning, and the first to rise from the dead, so that he is first in everything. It means the church belongs to him and he leads it.
entries.1:19: God was pleased for his full nature and fullness to dwell in Christ. It means Jesus is not a partial picture of God but the complete one.
entries.1:20: Through Christ's death on the cross, God made peace and is bringing everything in heaven and earth back together under him. It means reconciliation is God's initiative, accomplished at great cost.
entries.1:21: They were once estranged from God and hostile toward him because of their evil behavior, but now he has brought them back. It means their past separation has been genuinely reversed.
entries.1:22: Christ accomplished this through his physical death, so that they could stand before God holy, blameless, and free from accusation. It means their standing before God is secure because of what Christ did, not their own record.
entries.1:23: This holds true as long as they stay grounded in faith and don't drift from the hope of the good news, which has been proclaimed everywhere and which Paul serves. It means continuing in trust matters, and the message is for all people.
entries.1:24: Paul rejoices in his sufferings for their sake and sees his hardships as part of the ongoing cost of serving Christ's body, the church. It means suffering for others' spiritual good is real but not wasted.
entries.1:25: Paul became a servant of the church by God's assignment, given specifically to complete the task of proclaiming God's word. It means his role was God-given and aimed at their benefit.
entries.1:26: A mystery hidden for ages has now been revealed to God's people. It means God's long-hidden plan is no longer a secret; it has been made known.
entries.1:27: That revealed secret is Christ living in them, including non-Jewish believers, which is the sure hope of future glory. It means God's presence inside a person is the guarantee of what is to come.
entries.1:28: Paul and his coworkers proclaim Christ, teaching and guiding everyone with wisdom so that each person can become fully mature in him. It means the goal of teaching is complete growth, not just information.
entries.1:29: Paul works hard toward this goal, straining with all his energy, which is actually Christ's power at work in him. It means effort and dependence on God's strength go together, not one or the other.
entries.2:1: Paul wants his friends to know how hard he is working and praying for them, even though he has never met some of them. It means you are not forgotten by God's workers, even when you feel far away.
entries.2:2: Paul's goal is for them to be encouraged and knit together in love, so they can fully understand the wonderful truth that God's hidden plan is Christ himself. It means real comfort and confidence come from knowing Jesus better.
entries.2:3: Everything truly wise and worth knowing is stored up in Christ. It means you don't have to look elsewhere for the deepest answers to life; they are found in Jesus.
entries.2:4: Paul warns them so that smooth-talking people won't trick them with clever but false arguments. It means be careful of persuasive words that sound good but lead you away from the truth.
entries.2:5: Even though Paul is far away physically, he is with them in spirit and is glad to see their good order and steady faith in Christ. It means your faithfulness brings joy to those who care about you, even from a distance.
entries.2:6: Since you have received Jesus as Lord, keep living your life in him. It means the Christian life is a continuing walk with Jesus, not just a one-time start.
entries.2:7: Be like a tree with deep roots and a house built on a solid foundation, growing strong in the faith you were taught, and full of thankfulness. It means stay grounded in what you were taught and let gratitude shape your life.
entries.2:8: Watch out that no one captures you with empty philosophy and human traditions that are not based on Christ. It means don't let clever ideas or cultural trends pull you away from Jesus.
entries.2:9: The full nature of God truly lives in Christ in a real, bodily way. It means Jesus is not just a teacher or a picture of God; he is God himself among us.
entries.2:10: You have everything you need in Christ, who is above every power and authority. It means you don't need anything or anyone else to make you complete.
entries.2:11: In Christ you received a spiritual circumcision, which means your old sinful nature was cut away. It means following Christ brings a real inner change, not just an outward ritual.
entries.2:12: Baptism pictures being buried with Christ and raised to new life through faith in God's power that raised him from the dead. It means your new life rests on God's mighty work, not your own effort.
entries.2:13: You were spiritually dead because of your sins, but God gave you life with Christ and forgave all your sins. It means no sin is too much for God's forgiveness to cover.
entries.2:14: God canceled the record of debt that stood against us by nailing it to the cross. It means your guilt has been taken away, not ignored, but dealt with at the cross.
entries.2:15: On the cross Christ stripped the spiritual powers of their authority and publicly defeated them. It means the forces that once held you down have been beaten by Jesus.
entries.2:16: Don't let anyone judge you about what you eat or drink or which religious days you keep. It means your standing with God doesn't depend on keeping extra rules about food or calendars.
entries.2:17: Those rules were only a shadow pointing to what was coming; the real thing is Christ. It means the old rituals were pointers, and Jesus is the reality they pointed to.
entries.2:18: Don't let anyone cheat you out of your reward by pretending to be humble and worshiping angels, puffed up by visions and human ideas. It means beware of people who make spirituality complicated and push Christ aside.
entries.2:19: Such a person is not connected to Christ, the Head, from whom the whole body grows as God gives it strength. It means staying connected to Jesus is what makes you grow spiritually.
entries.2:20: If you died with Christ and are free from the world's basic rules, why live as if you still have to obey them? It means don't go back to rule-keeping as if that were the Christian life.
entries.2:21: These rules say don't handle, don't taste, don't touch. It means human-made restrictions about physical things don't make you more holy.
entries.2:22: Such rules are about things that perish with use and are merely human commands and teachings. It means rules made up by people have no lasting spiritual value.
entries.2:23: These rules look wise with their self-made religion, false humility, and harsh treatment of the body, but they have no real value in controlling sinful desires. It means looking strict on the outside doesn't change the heart.
entries.3:1: Since you've been given new life with Christ, aim your attention at heavenly things, where Christ rules. What you focus your mind on should reflect where your real life now belongs.
entries.3:2: Point your mind upward, not only at what is right in front of you. Attention shapes appetite.
entries.3:3: Your old earthly life has ended, and your true life is now hidden and safe with Christ in God. You don't need to prove it to anyone; God holds it securely.
entries.3:4: When Christ, who is your life, appears, you will appear with him in glory. Your future is tied to his, so what you endure now leads to sharing his honor.
entries.3:5: So treat your old earthly habits as dead: sexual sin, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is really idolatry. These things don't belong in the life you now have.
entries.3:6: God's anger comes on those who disobey him because of such practices. This is a serious warning about where those behaviors lead.
entries.3:7: You used to live that way when you did those things. It describes your past, not your present, so don't drift back into it.
entries.3:8: Now get rid of all of it: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy talk. These have no place in how you speak and treat others.
entries.3:9: Stop lying to each other, since you've taken off your old self with its habits. Honesty should mark your relationships now.
entries.3:10: You've put on a new self that is being renewed in knowledge to reflect its Maker. You are being changed to become more like the God who made you.
entries.3:11: In this new life there's no difference between Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free; Christ is everything and in everyone. No one is excluded or ranked above another in him.
entries.3:12: As God's chosen, holy, and dearly loved people, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. These qualities should shape how you treat people.
entries.3:13: Bear with each other and forgive whatever grievances you have, just as the Lord forgave you. Since you've been forgiven, extend that same forgiveness.
entries.3:14: Above all these, put on love, which binds everything together in perfect unity. Love is what holds all the other virtues together.
entries.3:15: Let Christ's peace rule in your hearts, since you were called into one body, and be thankful. Let peace, not conflict, guide your decisions and relationships.
entries.3:16: Let Christ's message dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing to God with gratitude. Fill your life with his word and let it overflow in worship together.
entries.3:17: Whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God through him. Every part of your life can be done as an offering to him.
entries.3:18: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. This calls for a respectful, ordered relationship within your commitment to Christ.
entries.3:19: Husbands, love your wives and don't be harsh with them. Your leadership is meant to be loving, not bitter or domineering.
entries.3:20: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord. Honoring your parents is part of following Christ.
entries.3:21: Fathers, don't provoke or embitter your children, so they don't become discouraged. Treat them in a way that builds them up rather than breaks their spirit.
entries.3:22: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not just when watched, but with sincerity and reverence for the Lord. Do your work honestly as service to Christ, not just to please people.
entries.3:23: Work as if God were the one you answer to. That changes the quality, not just the audience.
entries.3:24: You know the Lord will give you an inheritance as your reward; you are serving the Lord Christ. Your faithful work has a real reward from him, even if no one else notices.
entries.3:25: Anyone who does wrong will be repaid for that wrong, and there is no favoritism. God judges fairly and doesn't play favorites based on status.
entries.4:1: Masters must treat their servants fairly and equally, because they too have a Master in heaven who sees how they treat others. If you have any authority over people, treat them justly and remember God is watching you.
entries.4:2: Keep on praying at all times, staying alert and thankful as you do. Prayer should be a steady habit in your life, not just something for emergencies.
entries.4:3: Paul asks them to pray that God will open a door for the message about Christ to be preached, even though he is in chains for it. Pray for opportunities for God's word to spread, including through people who are suffering for it.
entries.4:4: Paul wants to explain the message clearly, as he should. Pray that those who speak about Christ will say it plainly and well.
entries.4:5: Act wisely toward people who don't believe, and make the most of every opportunity. How you live in front of outsiders matters, so use your time well.
entries.4:6: Let your words be kind and gracious, with a bit of salt, so you can give a good answer to anyone. Speak in a way that is pleasant and thoughtful, ready to respond to people who ask you questions.
entries.4:7: Tychicus, a dear brother and faithful helper, will tell them all the news about Paul. Good friends who serve faithfully are a gift, and it's good to share news through people you trust.
entries.4:8: Paul sent Tychicus so they could hear how Paul and his companions were doing and be encouraged. Sometimes a visit or a message from a trusted friend is exactly what lifts your heart.
entries.4:9: Onesimus, a beloved brother from their own city, is coming with Tychicus to tell them everything happening where Paul is. It's a comfort when someone you know personally brings you news and stands with you.
entries.4:10: Aristarchus, who is in prison with Paul, sends greetings, and so does Mark, Barnabas's relative; they should welcome Mark kindly if he comes. Even people who once failed can be restored, so receive them warmly.
entries.4:11: Jesus, also called Justus, sends greetings too; these are the only Jewish believers working with Paul for God's kingdom, and they have been a comfort to him. Faithful companions who stand with you in hard work are a real encouragement.
entries.4:12: Epaphras, one of their own, sends his love and constantly prays that they will be mature and fully sure of God's will. It's a blessing to have someone who prays for you to grow strong and confident in God.
entries.4:13: Paul testifies that Epaphras has worked hard and suffered much for them and for the believers in Laodicea and Hierapolis. Some people quietly pour out great effort for others, and that deserves to be recognized.
entries.4:14: Luke, the beloved doctor, and Demas send their greetings. Friends, including those with practical skills, are part of the fellowship and their greetings matter.
entries.4:15: Paul asks them to greet the brothers in Laodicea and Nymphas and the church that meets in their house. Small gatherings in homes were real churches, and greeting one another keeps believers connected.
entries.4:16: After this letter is read publicly, it should also be read in the church at Laodicea, and they should get the letter from Laodicea too. God's word is meant to be shared widely, not kept to one group.
entries.4:17: Tell Archippus to be sure he completes the work the Lord gave him. Whatever task God has entrusted to you, see it through faithfully.
entries.4:18: Paul writes this closing greeting in his own hand and reminds them he is a prisoner; he prays grace will be with them. Even in hard circumstances, he ends with love and a blessing, and we can do the same.
